body: Quick pass (UMA) @ 78f2f0a8: merges cleanly, quick gate green on head (+44 coolant/post/machine app suites run by hand since .cps changes aren't gate-mapped, #923), clippy clean, no golden moved, body complete, #869 not P?. Flagged ready for an independent review. Note for the reviewer and the cut: `feat(post)!`, since old Flood ops on an Air-only Carvera now refuse by name instead of posting M7.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 78f2f0a85501d6c32ce9fcfc8e7e83776c2b0524 -->
**Independent review (maintainer's reviewer, high tier: this changes posted coolant words). Verdict: no blockers - built and tested clean. It is a declared breaking change, so it waits for the maintainer to choose the cut that takes it (labelled `needs-maintainer`).**

### What breaks (for the maintainer)

| Area | Before | After | Breaking? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Project files | `coolant`: off / flood / mist / through-tool | adds `"air"`; no `PROJECT_VERSION` change | Old projects load unchanged. An **older build cannot open** a project holding an Air op (serde: unknown variant `air`, a clean load refusal). New ops on the shipped Carvera are Air by default, so any Carvera project saved with this build hits that. |
| Machine files (`.mch`) | - | no new key; reader unchanged | No. Existing files load and post the same, except the rows below. The **editor** now refuses to save a file holding a codeless coolant (see note 2). |
| Parameters / commands / MCP | - | nothing removed or renamed; `MachineDraft::add_coolant(name)` becomes `add_coolant(name, code)` (internal API) | No. |
| Flood op, shipped Carvera (`Air M7` only), `carvera.cps` | posted **M7** (first coded entry) | **refused by name** ("operation X: the machine states no flood coolant code - pick ... Air ...") | **Yes - the declared break.** One coolant pick per existing op. |
| Flood op, generic posts (Fanuc, Haas, 840D, Heidenhain, Mazak, Doosan, both lathes) on a machine whose only coolant is `Air`/`Air blast` | M7 ("Air" read as a shop's own flood name) | refused by name | Yes (no shipped machine pairs these). |
| Flood op, `tormach.cps`, machine listing only Mist (or Air) | posted the first coded entry (M7: mist/air for a flood ask) | refused by name | Yes - and a fix: that was a silent substitution. All shipped Tormach mills list Flood M8: unchanged. |
| Flood op, any machine with a `Flood` code (all other shipped machines) | M8 / M9 | M8 / M9 | No. Goldens byte-identical. |
| Flood op, Carvera profile with `Flood M8` + `Air M7` (the #869 report) | M8 | M8 (a Flood op); M7 for an Air op | No for Flood; Air is new. |
| Off / Mist / Through-tool op on `carvera.cps` | engine refusal (no `coolantModes`) | Off posts no coolant; Mist / Through-tool take their own entry or are refused by name | Relaxed, not broken. |

### Coolant output per post (checked in the scripts and by `coolant_air`)

- **Off**: nothing on every post. **Flood**: the `Flood` entry, else a shop's own coded name, else (list states only known other kinds) a named refusal; a codeless `Flood` stays the operator's own valve (silent, the #150 law); no list at all stays silent. **Mist**: `Mist` entry or refusal. **Air**: `Air` / `Air blast` entry or refusal. **Through tool**: `Through-spindle` / `Through-tool` entry or refusal. Same law in `carvera.cps` (now `coolantModes = true`) and the eight generic posts; `tormach.cps` reads no ask, so the engine refuses a non-Flood op there by name (pinned).
- No silent substitution: Air never takes a `Mist` entry and Flood never takes an `Air` entry, even when both are M7 - Air is its own family, so a machine with `Mist M7` + `Air M10` posts the right one. Every refusal names the operation. `message()` blocks the write in-app.
- M9 at section end and before M2 as before (`endPreamble`); the ask now resets to flood at section end on the Carvera, like the generic posts.
- **#995 (probe section starts flood): the same**, neither better nor worse. The Carvera refuses Probe ops outright; the generic posts' flood path is unchanged.

### What looks good

- `CoolantMode::machine_default` (crates/post/src/post/coolant.rs:108) mirrors the posts' flood law exactly, so a new op never starts on an ask its own machine would refuse. It is taken once in `CreateOperation::new` (crates/app/src/commands/operation/create.rs:109-111) and stored on the op: undo removes the op, redo replays the stored value, and changing the machine later does not change existing ops (their post refuses by name if they no longer fit). Every creation path (UI, MCP `create_operation`, pockets) goes through `CreateOperation::new`.
- The editor keeps unknown/extra coolant entries (the draft is the file's JSON value; only the removed entry is touched); `remove_coolant` (crates/app/src/machine/draft.rs:181) checks the pointer shape and bounds and refuses by name; `save()` now checks refusals like `save_as()`.
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests; no snapshot PNG or golden changed; no new crate dependency; decision file present; MCP follow-up #954 named; commit is `feat(post)!` with a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer. Files stay under 400 lines (draft.rs 280, machine_file_editor.rs 311, coolant.rs 119).

### Local results (trial merge with main a6bd69d8, clean, Windows)

|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-post` | lib 16, axis_direction_cli 3, comp 9, comp_plane 3, mch_head_search 2, post_engine 33 - all pass |
| app suites | coolant 7, coolant_air 4, coolant_followups 7, carvera_post 4, carvera_machines 1, fanuc_post 11, doosan_dnm_post 7, heidenhain_cycles 11, lathe_post 7, lathe_post_refusals 6, lathe_post_tormach 7, tormach_post 10, tormach_machines 6, tormach_lathes 2, sinumerik_safe_retract 3, posting 17, conformance 6, golden_cl 25, project_roundtrip 71, commands_undo 30, machine 33, machine_edit 12, machine_library 11, machine_assign 3, probe_op 12, probe_dialects 13, probe_tormach 7 - all pass |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` (CWD crates/ui) | 532 passed, 5 ignored |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

No CRLF-sensitive failures on this `core.autocrlf=true` checkout.

### Requested before merge

None.

### Notes (non-blocking)

1. **Changelog line**: it does not say "breaking". The release notes must lead with this change under 0.x; suggest starting the row with "Breaking: a Flood op on an Air-only machine (the shipped Carvera) is now refused by name - pick Air; ...".
2. **Editor vs. post law on codeless coolants**: the posts and the validator treat a stated codeless `Flood` as the operator's own valve, but the file editor now refuses to save any file that holds one (`codeless_coolants`, crates/app/src/machine/draft.rs:257). A user who opens an existing hand-written `.mch` with such an entry must code or remove it before Save. Deliberate per the decision file; worth a line in the release notes.
3. The mounted-machine editor (Setup pane) still adds a codeless coolant row (the PR body says so). Its behaviour now differs from the file editor; a small follow-up issue would keep them in step.
4. Remove buttons read "Remove Coolant Flood"; two coolants with the same name give two identical labels. Cosmetic.
5. On an Air-only machine posted through a generic post, a new Probe op would default to Air and so start the air blast in a probe section - the same class as #995, worth a line there when it is fixed. No shipped machine/post pair reaches it.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
